title: Vegetable couscous
intro: Fluffy couscous under vegetables and chickpeas simmered in a ras el hanout broth.

steps.t: Cut the carrots and turnip into thick sticks, the pumpkin and courgettes into 4 cm chunks, slice the onion, chop the tomatoes.
In a large pot, soften the onion in 2 tbsp oil with the ras el hanout, turmeric and ginger.
steps.label: Spices

steps.t: Add the tomatoes, carrots, turnip and hot stock (store-bought is fine). Salt and simmer for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Add the pumpkin, courgettes, chickpeas and raisins and cook for 15 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Meanwhile put the couscous in a bowl with 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp oil, pour over the boiling water and cover.
steps.label: Couscous

steps.t: Fluff the couscous with a fork, rubbing the grains so they stay separate.
Mound the couscous, arrange the vegetables and chickpeas on top, moisten with a ladle of broth and finish with herbs.

tips.t: Serve the extra broth in a jug on the side, with harissa for anyone who wants heat.
Not vegan: simmer 4 chicken legs in the broth from the start until fully cooked.

title: Barley orzotto with radicchio
intro: Pearl barley cooked like risotto, with red radicchio and wine: gently bitter and creamy.

steps.t: Rinse the barley. Shred the radicchio, keeping a little raw, and chop the shallot. Keep the stock hot (store-bought is fine).
Soften the shallot in the oil over low heat for 3 minutes, without browning.
steps.label: Shallot

steps.t: Add the barley and toast for 2 minutes, then pour in the red wine and let it evaporate.
steps.label: Toast

steps.t: Add the stock a ladle at a time and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Barley

pressure.t: Pour in 900 ml hot stock at once, lock the pressure cooker and cook for 15 minutes at pressure. Release.

steps.t: Add the radicchio and cook 10 more minutes, until the barley is tender but still slightly chewy.
steps.label: Radicchio

pressure.t: Open, add the radicchio and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, loosening with stock if needed.

steps.t: Turn off the heat, stir in the butter and Grana, season and let it rest for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Finish

steps.t: Serve topped with the toasted chopped walnuts and the reserved raw radicchio.

tips.t: Finish with 80 g taleggio or gorgonzola instead of Grana: it loves the bitterness.
Barley doesn't go mushy: next day, reheat it in a pan with a ladle of stock.

title: Farro salad with pesto
intro: Chewy farro with green beans, cherry tomatoes and pesto: make it ahead, take it anywhere.

steps.t: Boil the farro in plenty of salted water for the time on the pack, about 20 minutes, until tender but chewy.
steps.label: Farro

steps.t: Meanwhile trim the green beans and cut them in three. Add them to the farro pot for the last 7 minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until golden. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
steps.label: Pine nuts

steps.t: Save 3 tbsp cooking water, drain the farro and beans, spread them on a tray with the oil and leave to cool.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Loosen the pesto (homemade or from the chilled aisle) with the reserved water.
Combine the farro, beans, tomatoes and pesto, mix well and finish with pine nuts and basil. Serve at room temperature.

tips.t: Add 125 g mini mozzarella balls or tuna in oil to make it a full meal.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge: take it out 20 minutes ahead, as cold pesto loses aroma.

title: Quinoa with asparagus, peas and mint
intro: Fluffy quinoa with green spring vegetables, lemon, mint and toasted almonds.

steps.t: Rinse the quinoa well in a sieve under running water: it removes the bitter aftertaste.
Cook it covered in 480 ml salted water over low heat for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the germ shows.
steps.label: Quinoa

steps.t: Meanwhile snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut into 3 cm pieces, keeping the tips apart. Slice the spring onions.
Sauté the onions and stems in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, then the tips and peas with a splash of water for 3 more, until bright green.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden. Zest and juice the lemon.
Fluff the quinoa and fold in the vegetables, lemon zest and juice, remaining oil, torn mint, salt and pepper. Top with almonds.

tips.t: Not vegan: crumble 100 g feta or ricotta salata on top.
Great the next day as a packed lunch: add the mint only just before eating.

title: Turkish bulgur pilaf
intro: Coarse bulgur cooked with tomato and green peppers: Turkey's everyday side dish.

steps.t: Chop the onion, dice the peppers and grate the tomatoes, discarding the skins.
Soften the onion and peppers in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, then the grated tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Stir in the bulgur for 1 minute, then add the hot stock (store-bought is fine), salt, pepper and mint. Bring to the boil.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Turn off the heat, put a clean tea towel under the lid and rest for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Serve with cucumber yogurt (no longer vegan) or grilled vegetables.
Add 1 tsp Turkish pepper paste (biber salçası) with the tomato paste for a more authentic taste.

title: Polenta concia (cheesy polenta)
intro: Mountain polenta with stringy fontina and sage brown butter poured over the top.

steps.t: Bring the water to the boil with the salt. Pour in the cornmeal in a stream, whisking so no lumps form.
Cook over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon every few minutes, until it pulls away from the sides.
steps.label: Polenta

steps.t: Meanwhile dice the fontina and grate the Parmigiano.
Near the end, melt the butter with the sage over medium heat for 3 minutes, until foaming and hazelnut brown.
steps.label: Butter

steps.t: Take the polenta off the heat and stir in the fontina and Parmigiano until melted and stringy.
Serve in shallow bowls, pour over the sage butter and finish with black pepper.

tips.t: With instant polenta it takes just 8 minutes: less flavour, but still very good.
Leftovers set firm: slice them and grill or pan-fry until golden.
Serve with sautéed mushrooms or a meat stew.
